title: Удар по самолюбию и правки в меню  (Wounded Pride and Menu Adjustments)

segments.t: Stepping aside to answer Elena's call, Viktor Petrovich hears her declare that she has decided not to depend on men either because it is humiliating, before hanging up on him. Stung and distracted, the Chef returns to the table as the wedding clients begin listing changes to the banquet menu.
Я тоже решила от мужчин не зависеть.
Давай после поговорим, я сейчас немного занят.
Мы бы хотели немножко скорректировать меню.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'One second, this is very important.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'just a second' before landing on 'important'. Dmitry answers right away.
'Why do you keep hanging up on my calls?' The grammar packs 'you' and 'to reject a call' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Because I do not want to talk.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'want'.
'That is why I am calling you back.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'therefore' and 'to call back' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
Я тоже решила от мужчин не зависеть.
'I have also decided not to depend on men anymore.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'depends'.
'It is humiliating for a woman.' Notice how Russian expresses 'this' and 'woman' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'What was it you wanted to say?' Vika anchors the line on 'what', while 'say' completes the thought. Dmitry answers right away.
Давай после поговорим, я сейчас немного занят.
'Let us talk later, I am a bit busy right now.' In Russian, the idea of 'let's' flows naturally into 'busy' without extra filler words.
'Forgive me, let us get started.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'excuse me' before landing on 'to start'.
Мы бы хотели немножко скорректировать меню.
'We would like to make a few adjustments to the menu.' Notice how Russian expresses 'we' and 'menu' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'Alright then, go ahead.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'so' and finishing on 'like this'.
'Yes, all of that is completely fine.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'this' in a few short words.
'All of that is fine. Ah.' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'and' in spoken Russian. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Я тоже решила от мужчин не зависеть.
Давай после поговорим, я сейчас немного занят.
Мы бы хотели немножко скорректировать меню.
